title: Fnideq gathering over economic hardship and the closure of Bab Sebta
scope: A city-level gathering; the reviewed evidence does not establish other sites for this episode.
threshold_50_evidence: The opened CNDH annual report confirms a gathering but gives no attendance. Search-only coverage uses the ambiguous phrase “plusieurs dizaines”; the ≥50 threshold remains unverified.

title.summary: The CNDH report describes a Fnideq gathering protesting economic and social conditions after the closure of Bab Sebta.

start_date.summary: The CNDH report dates the gathering to 5 February 2021.

end_date.summary: No physical end date or time is stated.

location.summary: The report locates the gathering in Fnideq.

scope.summary: The cited passage concerns Fnideq; it does not identify other locations as part of this event.

organizer.summary: The reviewed passage names no organizer.

demands.summary: Participants protested economic and social conditions associated with the Bab Sebta closure and COVID-19 effects and demanded economic alternatives; no demand category is assigned.

participants.summary: The opened report gives no crowd size; the threshold is unresolved.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: The opened report gives no attendance figure. A different search-only report says “plusieurs dizaines,” which is not sufficient to establish at least 50.

protester_violence.summary: The CNDH describes a peaceful demonstration; TelQuel retrospectively says the preceding gathering ended in a riot. The accounts conflict, so violence remains unknown.

state_response.summary: The CNDH says local authorities dispersed the gathering and some participants were arrested. No other coded response dimension is established in the reviewed passage.

notes: The CNDH passage reports four people prosecuted; this is not a crowd count. TelQuel’s February 15 body describes the February 5 gathering retrospectively as ending in a riot, while the CNDH calls it peaceful; preserve this discrepancy. No body review was completed for the Chamaly item found in search results.
open_questions: Can a reviewed source establish attendance of at least 50?
What was the gathering’s physical end time?
Can the conflicting characterization of violence be resolved with independent event-specific reporting?

title: Fnideq sit-in demanding the reopening of Bab Sebta
location: The main square and area around Mohammed V mosque, Fnideq, Morocco
scope: A local gathering in Fnideq; no other sites are combined.
participants_original: The opened article says hundreds gathered around the Mohammed V mosque.
threshold_50_evidence: The opened article describes “des centaines” of people gathered near the Mohammed V mosque, supporting a size above 50; it gives no exact count or bounded range.

title.summary: The article describes Fnideq’s second demonstration and sit-in demanding the reopening of Bab Sebta.

start_date.summary: The article identifies the demonstration as occurring on Friday, 12 February 2021.

end_date.summary: The reviewed public text gives no physical end date or time.

location.summary: The article places the sit-in at the main square and describes hundreds gathered around Mohammed V mosque in Fnideq.

scope.summary: The article describes the Fnideq gathering only.

organizer.summary: No organizer is identified in the reviewed public text.

demands.summary: Participants demanded reopening Bab Sebta; no original category is assigned.

participants.summary: The article says hundreds gathered but supplies no exact count.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: The phrase “des centaines” supports at least 50 attendees, without establishing a precise number.

protester_violence.summary: The article mentions a few incidents of disorder but does not attribute them to protesters or describe violence clearly; unknown.

state_response.summary: The reviewed public text does not establish event-specific state action for this gathering; unknown.

notes: The article’s characterization of the 5 February gathering as ending in a riot conflicts with the CNDH report’s description of that earlier demonstration as peaceful; this does not establish violence at the 12 February sit-in. The remainder of the TelQuel page is behind a subscription wall, so coding is limited to the reviewed public text.
open_questions: What was the gathering’s physical end time?
Was there any event-specific state response?
Can the few reported incidents of disorder be attributed and characterized?

title: Rabat gathering for the 20 February Movement anniversary prevented by authorities
scope: One intended local sit-in/gathering in Rabat; no other city or anniversary action is combined.
participants_original: “العشرات من النشطاء” (dozens of activists), as reported.
threshold_50_evidence: The article says “dozens of activists,” which does not establish a minimum of 50 or a numeric range; threshold remains unresolved.

title.summary: The report describes a Social Front sit-in for the 20 February anniversary that authorities prevented in Rabat.

start_date.summary: The article is dated 20 February 2021 at 17:30 and describes that Saturday evening.

end_date.summary: No physical end date or time is stated; null is unknown.

location.summary: The article locates the activists at Bab al-Had square in Rabat.

scope.summary: Only the Rabat gathering is described; no other city event is included.

organizer.summary: The article identifies the Social Front as the sit-in organizer.

demands.summary: The gathering commemorated the 20 February movement; the broader Moroccan Association for Human Rights demand list in the same article is not attributed to these attendees, so no demand category is assigned.

participants.summary: The report says “dozens of activists” gathered, without an exact number or interval.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: “Dozens” does not establish at least 50; attendance threshold remains unresolved.

protester_violence.summary: The inspected passage reports no protester violence; no explicit peacefulness finding is coded, so unknown.

state_response.summary: Authorities prevented the sit-in. The report says security pushed demonstrators and some activists said they were kicked; beatings are coded yes as reported allegation, not independently verified in this excerpt.

notes: Keep this Rabat event separate from anniversary leads in Zaio, Beni Mellal, Khenifra and other cities. The report’s “dozens” is not a numeric lower bound of 50. The broader demands statement is not attributed to the attendees. Reported kicking is attributed to statements by some activists, not independently confirmed in the reviewed lines.
open_questions: Can body-verified attendance establish at least 50?
What were the onsite group’s explicit demands beyond the anniversary context?
What was the physical end time?
Can the reported kicking be independently corroborated?
